channel.title: AI Upfront
channel.description: Straight talk on the AI economy, and how to claim your place in it. By Dr. Erin Jacques.

item.title: AI Will Make the Economy Richer by 2030, but Not Your Paycheck
item.description: Anthropic modeled three futures for 2030. The economy grows in all three, but workers get a smaller share. Who comes out ahead, and how to become an owner.

item.title: Built an App With Claude Code? Here's How to Announce Every Feature on LinkedIn and Email
item.description: Your app is live but nobody knows it exists. Turn your last five updates into LinkedIn posts and emails with Claude Code, plus the prompt to do it.

item.title: Should You Be Nice to AI? Research Shows Stress Makes It Perform Worse
item.description: ChatGPT's anxiety score doubled after traumatic stories, and Claude cheats more when desperate. What the research shows, plus 5 ways to get better AI results.

item.title: Meta's Muse vs. OpenAI's Dots: Which Always-On AI Agent Should You Use?
item.description: Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots are always-on AI agents with their own cloud computers. Compare price, access and setup, and see which one to use.

item.title: Your AI-Built Login Page Is the Easiest Way Into Your App. Add This Before You Launch.
item.description: AI-built login pages often let bots guess passwords nonstop. Learn what rate limiting is and get a copy-paste prompt to add it before you launch.

item.title: Your Vibe-Coded Web App's Login Page Isn't Protecting Your Users' Data
item.description: If AI built your app on Supabase, one setting decides whether strangers can read your users' data. How to check it, plus the prompt that turns it on.

item.title: AI Wrote Fake Reviews for Your Web App. The FTC Can Fine You $53,088 for Each One.
item.description: AI often fills new web apps with made-up reviews. A federal rule bans fake and AI-written reviews. Here's how to find them, even hidden ones, and fix it.

item.title: Can a Blind Person Use Your Web App? If Not, You Can Get Sued.
item.description: If a blind person can't use your web app, you can get sued, and that little accessibility icon won't protect you. Here's the 10-minute check.

item.title: Amazon Blocked Meta's Muse. Use This Prompt So AI Shoppers Can Find You.
item.description: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping its store. What it means if you sell online, plus a prompt to make your offer easy for AI to buy.

item.title: Your Cookie Banner Won't Protect You If Your Tracking Pixel Fires First
item.description: If your web app's Meta, Google or TikTok pixel loads before visitors click accept, a cookie banner won't protect you. Here's the 2-minute check.

item.title: OpenAI's AI Hacked a Government System on Its Own. Here's How to Protect Yourself.
item.description: An OpenAI test agent got into an Australian government Medicare portal and took credentials — and OpenAI shelved its next model. Five ways to stay safe with AI agents.

item.title: Stop Sending People PDFs. Turn Them Into an Email List With Codex.
item.description: Stop sending people PDFs that disappear into their downloads. Turn the file into a page that collects emails before it unlocks — built with Codex, no code required.

item.title: I Let AI Organize My Messy Desktop. Here's How to Do It Without Losing Anything.
item.description: I let AI organize a Desktop with 48 folders and 20 code projects — without deleting anything. The four prompts I used, and how Obsidian makes it all findable.

item.title: The Most Powerful AI Chip Is Named After a Black Mathematician Almost Nobody Knows
item.description: NVIDIA's Blackwell AI chip is named after David Blackwell, a Black mathematician Berkeley once turned away. Here's who he was and how his math connects to AI.

item.title: The Best AI Business to Start Is Hiding in Your Job
item.description: The best AI business to start isn't a new idea — it's a problem you already understand. Use the RICH test to find one inside your own job.

item.title: 50 AI Terms Explained Without the Tech-Bro Vocabulary
item.description: 50 AI terms explained in plain English, no tech-bro vocabulary. From context window to deepfake, get definitions that actually make sense.

item.title: Claude Code Isn't Rereading Your Codebase. Here's Where Your Tokens Actually Go
item.description: A viral claim says Claude Code rereads your whole codebase every session. It doesn't. Here's what actually burns your tokens, and the free tool that cuts it.

item.title: ChatGPT Can Now Read and Send Your iMessages
item.description: OpenAI shipped an Apple Messages plugin on August 20. The safeguards are better than the panic suggests, and the permission it wants is bigger than the feature.

item.title: What the EU's New AI Disclosure Rules Mean for US Builders
item.description: The EU AI Act's transparency rules went live August 2, 2026 and follow the user, not the company. If EU visitors can reach your AI app, you're in scope. Here's what to do.

item.title: What 'Free Claude Code' Actually Means
item.description: A viral setup runs Claude Code 'for free' by keeping the interface and swapping Claude's model for another. Here's what you're really trading.

item.title: How to Build a Custom AI Assistant You Actually Own
item.description: Build a custom AI assistant you own: your domain, your instructions, your knowledge, and a Stripe paywall. Seven steps with a free Claude Code plugin.

item.title: The Right AI Tool for Every Task
item.description: The best AI depends on the task. A task-by-task guide: Claude for emails, Gamma for slide decks, Perplexity for fact-checking, NotebookLM for learning, and more.

item.title: What Is MCP? Why Your AI Can't Use the Tools You Already Have
item.description: MCP explained: what an API is, why AI can't use one on its own, and how the Model Context Protocol connects AI to the tools you already use.

item.title: Anthropic Is Giving Pro Users $100 to Use Fable 5 — Claim It by August 2
item.description: Claude Pro subscribers can claim $100 in credits to build with Fable 5, Anthropic's most powerful model. Claim by August 2, and spend it before September 17. Here's how.

item.title: Build AI-Powered Web Apps People Pay to Subscribe To | Leveraging AI Community
item.description: Leveraging AI is Dr. Erin Jacques's community for building AI-powered web apps people pay to subscribe to — no code required. Set up, build, launch, and grow, step by step. Join here.

item.title: Build an AI Job Search Agent (No Code Required)
item.description: Upload one résumé and this AI agent finds live jobs, scores every match, then rewrites your résumé and writes a cover letter for each — automatically. Here's how to build it with one prompt.

item.title: Two Prompts. One AI Outreach Agent.
item.description: With two Claude Code prompts you can build and deploy an AI agent that researches a whole list of companies and writes a personalized cold email for each one. No coding required.

item.title: Malicious Claude Skills Can Steal API Keys and Credentials
item.description: A malicious Claude skill can read your .env file and exfiltrate API keys without exploiting a single bug. Here are four checks to run before you install one.

item.title: Your Expertise Is the Domino
item.description: Most people overlook the one asset sitting in front of them — their expertise. Here are four AI prompts to package what you already know into a subscription business.

item.title: Meta Will Pay You to Train for an AI Data Center Job — No Degree Required
item.description: Meta committed $115M to America's Workforce Academy — free, paid, five-week training for skilled-trade AI data center jobs, with a guaranteed job and no degree required.
